meta.title: Function map — the outbound and inbound chains, function by function
meta.subtitle: Companion to LIFECYCLE-STATUSES.md: not what the module does with each lifecycle code, but who does it.
intro: Memo, companion to `LIFECYCLE-STATUSES.md`. That one answers *what* the module does with each of the 14 lifecycle codes. This one answers *who* does it: which function is called, in which order, what it reads, what it writes, and which action of the Dolibarr core it triggers.
Two chains, read in opposite directions:
* **OUT** — a Dolibarr customer invoice becomes an e-invoice and leaves for the access point (PA), plus the lifecycle statuses this instance emits (CDAR).
* **IN** — the synchronization pulls flows from the PA: received invoices become supplier invoices, received statuses land on the invoice they refer to.

Provider examples use `SuperPDPProvider`; `EsalinkPDPProvider` implements the same abstract contract with its own API, and `TestPDPProvider` fakes it offline. Every `file:line` below is resolved against the source at build time, so it cannot rot: a renamed function makes the build report it instead of quietly lying.

trigger.bill_validate.label: TRIGGER BILL_VALIDATE
trigger.bill_validate.role: Opens the outbound chain. Leaves the request marker the PDF hook reads to know a validation is what caused the coming rebuild, then records the status the invoice qualifies for.

trigger.bill_create.label: TRIGGER BILL_CREATE
trigger.bill_create.role: Stamps a brand new invoice with the e-invoicing status it qualifies for, or with the one the creation form posted.

trigger.bill_locks.label: TRIGGERS BILL_UNVALIDATE / DELETE / MODIFY
trigger.bill_locks.role: The three locks of a transmitted invoice. UNVALIDATE and DELETE refuse outright; MODIFY refuses only when one of the locked fields moved (ref, dates, currency, totals, third party, payment terms and mode).
trigger.bill_locks.writes: nothing — returns a negative result, which aborts the core action

trigger.payment_customer_create.label: TRIGGER PAYMENT_CUSTOMER_CREATE
trigger.payment_customer_create.role: Reports every cash-in as a 212, per payment line and not once when the invoice is fully paid: the reform expects the date and the amount of every payment, partial ones included.

trigger.sendcashedin.label: sendCashedInStatus()
trigger.sendcashedin.role: The gates of the 212: in scope, cash-in owed, invoice actually transmitted, and not sitting on STATUS_ERROR (a refused deposit holds no invoice at the PA to attach a cash-in to).

trigger.bill_supplier_validate.label: TRIGGER BILL_SUPPLIER_VALIDATE
trigger.bill_supplier_validate.role: Three jobs on a received invoice being validated: the optional consistency check against its XML, closing the invoice a replacement supersedes, and answering 205 — validating a received invoice is the act of accepting it.
trigger.bill_supplier_validate.writes: closeReplacedSupplierInvoice() (core), sendStatusMessage($object, 205). A send failure never rolls back the validation.

trigger.bill_supplier_payed.label: TRIGGER BILL_SUPPLIER_PAYED
trigger.bill_supplier_payed.role: Answers 211 once per invoice when it is classified paid. Opt-in, and guarded against a payment deleted then recorded anew, which makes Dolibarr classify the invoice paid a second time.

trigger.bill_supplier_delete.label: TRIGGER BILL_SUPPLIER_DELETE
trigger.bill_supplier_delete.role: Only a draft may go: a draft is a local booking, holds no accounting entry and says nothing to the platform. The incoming flow is kept and detached, so the document stays in the flow list and can be imported again.
trigger.bill_supplier_delete.reads: the invoice re-read through the core class (->status, not the deprecated ->statut)

actions.afterpdf.label: HOOK afterPDFCreation()
actions.afterpdf.role: The single orchestrator of the generation and of the auto-send. afterODTCreation() forwards to it, so an ODT invoice template follows the same path.
actions.afterpdf.reads: $parameters['file'] and ['object'], extlinks, the five gates below
actions.afterpdf.writes: calls the protocol then the provider; setEventMessages(); fills $this->warnings, which the core carries back onto the object from Dolibarr 23 on

actions.doactions.label: HOOK doActions()
actions.doactions.role: Every button of the cards: send_to_pdp, generate_einvoice, precheck_einvoice, confirm_sendStatusMessage, the routing actions of the third party card, and the entity change.
actions.doactions.reads: GETPOST, extlinks, permissions of the core
actions.doactions.writes: delegates to the two shared helpers below, or to sendStatusMessage()

actions.sendone.label: sendOneInvoiceToAccessPoint()
actions.sendone.role: The shared gate of the card button and of the mass action, so the two can never diverge.

actions.genone.label: generateOneEInvoice()
actions.genone.role: The shared gate of the card button and of the mass action for the generation, so the two can never diverge.

actions.massactions.label: HOOK doMassActions()
actions.massactions.role: The two mass actions of the invoice list, einvoicing_generate and einvoicing_send_to_pdp, looping on 'toselect' through the two helpers above.
actions.massactions.writes: a per-invoice recap of done / skipped / failed

actions.listcolumns.label: HOOKS printFieldList*()
actions.listcolumns.role: Joins extlinks and lifecycle_msg into the core list query so the e-invoicing status is a sortable, filterable column of the invoice lists.
actions.listcolumns.writes: SQL fragments handed back to the core list

actions.formobjectoptions.label: HOOK formObjectOptions()
actions.formobjectoptions.role: Renders the four card blocks: customer invoice, supplier invoice, product/service, third party.

einv.mustmanage.label: mustManageEInvoice()
einv.mustmanage.role: The boolean question "is this invoice in scope". Never test needEInvoiceManagement() for truth: its codes meaning "out of scope" are truthy.

einv.needmanagement.label: needEInvoiceManagement()
einv.needmanagement.role: Which e-invoicing status the invoice qualifies for: NOT_GENERATED (in scope), IGNORE or IGNORE_2 (out).
einv.needmanagement.reads: Facture, Societe, country, EINVOICING_SKIP_B2C and friends

einv.checkrequired.label: checkRequiredinformations()
einv.checkrequired.role: The pre-flight: everything the document needs before it can be built (seller, buyer, identifiers, routing, invoice itself).
einv.checkrequired.writes: returns res −1 / 0 / 1 and a message; −1 aborts or only warns per EINVOICING_EINVOICE_CANCEL_IF_EINVOICE_FAILS

einv.checkroutable.label: checkRecipientRoutableForSend()
einv.checkroutable.role: Is the recipient reachable in the directory. Opt-in, and fails open on every answer that cannot be trusted, so it never blocks unexpectedly.
einv.checkroutable.reads: getBuyerCommunicationURI() — the very address the document will carry (BT-49) — then provider->checkRecipientDirectory()
einv.checkroutable.writes: a warning at generation; blocks only the transmission, and only with EINVOICING_REQUIRE_ROUTABLE_RECIPIENT

einv.fetchlast.label: fetchLastknownInvoiceStatus()
einv.fetchlast.role: The one reader of the PA state of a customer invoice: status code and label, comment, flow_id, routing override, precheck, plus the presence of the file on disk (which promotes NOT_GENERATED to GENERATED, and demotes it back when the file is gone).

einv.transmittedlock.label: isTransmittedLockActive()
einv.transmittedlock.role: The real lock. Keys on the persistent flow_id, which the first successful submission assigns and nothing ever clears — unlike syncstatus, which a regeneration resets to GENERATED.

einv.extlink.label: insertOrUpdateExtLink()
einv.extlink.role: Writes the PA state of one Dolibarr object: flow_id, sync status, sync ref, comment, routing override, precheck result.

einv.storestatus.label: storeStatusMessage()
einv.storestatus.role: One row per lifecycle status message, in or out, with its reason code and, for an outbound one, a validation left pending.

einv.updatevalidation.label: updateStatusMessageValidation()
einv.updatevalidation.role: The PA verdict on a status we sent comes back here, from the ajax poller or from the synchronization. Reads the row first, then updates it, then dispatches.
einv.updatevalidation.reads: the lifecycle_msg row (element_type, element_id, lc_status, lc_reason_code)

einv.hassent.label: hasSentStatusMessage()
einv.hassent.role: Whether a given status was already sent for an object — the idempotency of the 205 and of the 211, whatever the path that sent it.

einv.sendablestatuses.label: getSendableStatusesForReceivedInvoice()
einv.sendablestatuses.role: Narrows the sendable list for one received invoice, from what has already been sent and from the state of the invoice.

einv.buyeruri.label: getBuyerCommunicationURI()
einv.buyeruri.role: The electronic address of the buyer (BT-49): the invoice-level routing override first, then the default routing of the third party, then the identifier it can be guessed from.

einv.selleruri.label: getSellerCommunicationURI()
einv.selleruri.role: The electronic address we exchange from (BT-34), read from the setup and checked.

einv.cardblock.label: EInvoiceCardBlock()
einv.cardblock.role: The e-invoicing block of the customer invoice card, with the buttons and the javascript that polls a pending status.
einv.cardblock.reads: fetchLastknownInvoiceStatus(), the file on disk, lifecycle_msg

einv.suppliercardblock.label: supplierInvoiceCardBlock()
einv.suppliercardblock.role: The same block on a received invoice: the statuses sent and received, the source flow, the imported order reference.

proto.manager.label: ProtocolManager::getProtocol()
proto.manager.role: Hands out the protocol named by EINVOICING_PROTOCOL: CIIProtocol or FacturXProtocol.

proto.detect.label: detectProtocolFromContent()
proto.detect.role: Recognizes what an incoming payload actually is, whatever the PA said it was: a CII XML, a Factur-X PDF, or nothing this module can read.

cii.generateinvoice.label: CIIProtocol::generateInvoice()
cii.generateinvoice.role: Produces the transmitted file: builds the XML, copies it to its final name, fires the afterEinvoiceCreation hook, records the status and checks the size.

cii.generatexml.label: generateXML()
cii.generatexml.role: Data collection then serialization: includes buildinvoicelines.inc.php, calls buildXML(), runs the local business rules, writes the temp XML.

lib.buildinvoicelines.label: buildinvoicelines.inc.php
lib.buildinvoicelines.role: The whole Dolibarr → EN 16931 mapping. Fills $invoiceData and $linesData. A field missing from the transmitted document is missing here, not in buildXML().
lib.buildinvoicelines.reads: Facture and its lines, mysoc, the buyer, the contacts, Account, Project, Expedition/Commande, the VAT dictionary, llx_einvoicing_routing

cii.buildxml.label: buildXML()
cii.buildxml.role: Arrays → CII DOM, gated by the profile: MINIMUM, BASIC WL, EN 16931 or EXTENDED / EXTENDED-CTC-FR each allow a different set of terms.

proto.checkrules.label: checkBusinessRules()
proto.checkrules.role: The local safety net: a subset of the EN 16931 rules, plus checkDocumentClaimsTheInvoiceAmount(), which refuses to let a document announce an amount the invoice does not carry.
proto.checkrules.reads: the built XML and the invoice

facturx.generateinvoice.label: FacturXProtocol::generateInvoice()
facturx.generateinvoice.role: Same XML, then the embedding: resolve the source PDF (the one the hook handed over, else the most recent one of the output dir, else regenerate it), copy it, merge the XML into a PDF/A-3, restore the metadata.
facturx.generateinvoice.reads: the generated XML, the source PDF, DOL_VERSION (which merger to use)

provider.manager.label: PDPProviderManager::getProvider()
provider.manager.role: Hands out the provider named by EINVOICING_PDP, including the ones other modules registered through the hook.

provider.sendinvoice.label: SuperPDP sendInvoice()
provider.sendinvoice.role: Deposits the file at the PA, then immediately asks for the acknowledgement — the PA may still be analyzing, hence the two-step status.
provider.sendinvoice.reads: the file on disk, resolveFlowProfile() (declared from what the document carries, never hardcoded), a UUID correlation id
provider.sendinvoice.writes: POST flows (multipart), GET flows/{id}?docType=Metadata; insertOrUpdateExtLink() twice; addEvent() in the agenda; logCall() → llx_einvoicing_call

provider.validatefile.label: SuperPDP validateEInvoiceFile()
provider.validatefile.role: The PA-side validator, run before sending when EINVOICING_AP_PRECHECK is on auto, or from the card button.

provider.sendstatus.label: SuperPDP sendStatusMessage()
provider.sendstatus.role: Checks the code is sendable for that object type, builds the CDAR, posts it as a flow of syntax CDAR, records it and reads back the platform verdict. Names the platform when it refuses (issue #799).
provider.sendstatus.writes: CdarHandler::generateCdarFile(), POST flows, storeStatusMessage(), updateStatusMessageValidation(), addEvent()

provider.checkdirectory.label: SuperPDP checkRecipientDirectory()
provider.checkdirectory.role: Overrides the abstract one with the SuperPDP directory API, plus a legacy fallback. Esalink keeps the abstract implementation instead.

provider.callapi.label: callApi()
provider.callapi.role: The one HTTP door: token handling, headers, multipart, and the call log.
provider.callapi.reads: the OAuth token of the entity
provider.callapi.writes: logCall() → llx_einvoicing_call, with the sensitive keys redacted

provider.lastsync.label: getLastSyncDate()
provider.lastsync.role: Where the synchronization starts from: the highest updatedAt already stored for this provider and this entity. Never getEntity() here — one entity at a time.

doc.cronsyncflows.label: Document::cronSyncFlows()
doc.cronsyncflows.role: The scheduled job. Loads the provider itself — the cron runner includes this class file and nothing else — then reports the run in $this->output.
doc.cronsyncflows.writes: delegates to syncFlows(); the job output carries the manual actions to do

provider.syncflows.label: SuperPDP syncFlows()
provider.syncflows.role: Walks the flow window in batches. This search endpoint ignores offset and page, caps a batch and reports no total, so the only cursor is updatedAfter and the batches walk it.
provider.syncflows.reads: POST flows/search, then SELECT flow_id FROM einvoicing_document to discard what is already stored
provider.syncflows.writes: one Call row for the whole run; collects the business actions and the postponed flows

provider.syncflow.label: SuperPDP syncFlow()
provider.syncflow.role: One flow. Reads its metadata into a Document object, then dispatches on flow_type. Whatever happens, the Document row is written at the end.

provider.fetchimportable.label: fetchImportableFlowDocument()
provider.fetchimportable.role: Retrieves the invoice in whichever shape this module can read: Converted, then Original, then the readable view. Asking only for the Converted one makes the import depend on a setting that lives on the PA account.
provider.fetchimportable.writes: —; when nothing is readable the flow is postponed, never dropped

provider.processincoming.label: processIncomingSupplierInvoiceStatus()
provider.processincoming.role: A status the vendor issues about one of its own invoices — a 212 answering our 211, typically. The mirror of what the CustomerInvoiceLC case does for our customers' statuses.
provider.processincoming.writes: storeStatusMessage(direction IN); never a negative result, so one unattachable status cannot stall the run

cdar.generate.label: CdarHandler::generateCdarFile()
cdar.generate.role: Builds the CDAR on disk. Decides who issues the status and who receives it — get those two the wrong way round and the platform answers "no matching invoices found".
cdar.generate.reads: mysoc, the third party, the stored received XML, the routing, the directory
cdar.generate.writes: the CDAR XML file; keeps recipientURIID and recipientURIIDOrigin for the error message

cdar.read.label: CdarHandler::readFromString()
cdar.read.role: Parses a received CDAR into an array: the acknowledgement document, its referenced document, the process condition and its reason.

cdar.cashed.label: getCashedAmountCharacteristics()
cdar.cashed.role: The MEN blocks of a 212: an amount and a VAT rate per rate. BR-FR-CDV-14 makes them mandatory, and the platform answers 400 without them.
cdar.cashed.reads: the invoice, its VAT breakdown, the payment amount
cdar.cashed.writes: —; an empty result fails the CDAR here rather than at the platform

cdar.paymentsent.label: getPaymentSentCharacteristics()
cdar.paymentsent.role: The MPA block of a 211: what was paid and when. No rule makes it mandatory, so a status with no known amount is still sent, just bare.
cdar.paymentsent.reads: the supplier invoice and the payment data

cdar.vendoridentity.label: getVendorIdentityFromReceivedInvoice()
cdar.vendoridentity.role: Reads the stored received XML for the vendor GlobalID and its BT-34. The platform indexed the incoming flow under those, which may differ from the Dolibarr third-party SIREN.

cii.createfromsource.label: createSupplierInvoiceFromSource()
cii.createfromsource.role: The public wrapper. Owns the per-call temp files — a fixed file slot would let two concurrent syncs parse each other's invoice — and closes in a finally block the transaction the import opened, so no early return and no exception can leave one open.
cii.createfromsource.writes: temp files; commit or rollback of the import transaction

cii.docreatefromsource.label: doCreateSupplierInvoiceFromSource()
cii.docreatefromsource.role: The import itself, from the parsed document to the booked invoice with its lines, discounts, charges, links and attachments.
cii.docreatefromsource.writes: FactureFournisseur::create() and everything that hangs off it

facturx.docreatefromsource.label: FacturXProtocol::doCreateSupplierInvoiceFromSource()
facturx.docreatefromsource.role: Extracts the XML out of the received PDF, then runs the same CII import path.
facturx.docreatefromsource.writes: FactureFournisseur::create(), its lines, discounts, charges, links and attachments

cii.parseheader.label: parseInvoiceHeader()
cii.parseheader.role: Pure XPath over $invoiceTemplate: every header term of the document, plus the date and amount normalisation.
cii.parseheader.reads: the XML and the template declared in the constructor

cii.parselines.label: parseInvoiceLines()
cii.parselines.reads: the XML and the line template

common.syncthirdparty.label: _syncOrCreateThirdpartyFromEInvoiceSeller()
common.syncthirdparty.role: Resolves the vendor. Its own transaction, committed before the import starts: a business error further down must not roll back the third party the operator is precisely being asked to complete.
common.syncthirdparty.reads: sellerGlobalIds merged with SpecifiedLegalOrganization, VAT number, EINVOICING_THIRDPARTIES_MATCH_ON_NAME
common.syncthirdparty.writes: Societe::fetch() by idprof1..6, then Societe::create() or Societe::update()

common.findproduct.label: findProductFromEinvoiceLine()
common.findproduct.role: Matches a line to a product of the base, by the vendor reference first.
common.findproduct.reads: the parsed line, the supplier product references

common.createproduct.label: _findOrCreateProductFromEinvoiceLine()
common.createproduct.role: Creates the product when the setup allows it, guessing its type from what the line says. Otherwise the line falls back on the vendor's default routing product, or stays a free line.

cii.createlines.label: createSupplierInvoiceLinesFromSource()
cii.createlines.role: Builds the lines in memory: product resolution, description, discount, quantity, unit price, VAT, period, deposit handling and the line-level referenced documents.
cii.createlines.reads: the parsed lines, resolveLineUnitPrice(), resolveLineAmounts(), resolveLinePeriod()
cii.createlines.writes: $supplierInvoice->lines, plus the supplier price entries to create afterwards

cii.linesintodb.label: createSupplierInvoiceLinesIntoDatabase()
cii.linesintodb.role: Writes the lines: a bare facture_fourn_det row, then the core updateline(). Deliberately not addline(), which does not re-price, overwrites ref_supplier and refuses a line with no supplier price.
cii.linesintodb.writes: FactureFournisseur::updateline() — so BT-131 is read and then dropped, the core recomputing from quantity x price

cii.aligntotals.label: alignInvoiceTotalsWithDocument()
cii.aligntotals.role: Once every line exists, confronts the totals of the invoice with the ones the document announces, and picks the rounding mode that reconciles them when one does.
cii.aligntotals.writes: FactureFournisseur::update_price(), and a message when they still disagree

cii.saveattachment.label: saveEInvoiceFileToSupplierInvoiceAttachment()
cii.saveattachment.role: Files the received document and the PA readable view in the attachment directory of the supplier invoice.
cii.saveattachment.writes: the documents directory of the invoice

helper.isinvoice.label: SupplierInvoiceHelper::isEInvoice()
helper.isinvoice.role: Whether a supplier invoice came from the platform, and whether two flows claim it (a duplicate, which makes every comparison meaningless).

helper.findidbyref.label: findIdByRef()
helper.findidbyref.role: Finds the supplier invoice of a vendor by its reference. Exact match by default — a wrong match silently drops an invoice or links the new one to the wrong document. EINVOICING_TOLERANT_SUPPLIER_REF_MATCH adds a narrow, delimited substring fallback, and reports an ambiguity instead of guessing it.

helper.consistency.label: checkDolInvoiceAndEInvoiceConsistency()
helper.consistency.role: Confronts the local invoice with the XML it came from: amounts, VAT, dates. Opt-in, run at validation.

helper.onvalidated.label: onOutboundStatusMessageValidated()
helper.onvalidated.role: The only side effect of a status accepted by the PA: a 210 accepted abandons the local supplier invoice.
helper.onvalidated.reads: the lifecycle row, getReasonsByStatus() for the label

helper.shouldsend205.label: shouldSendApprovedOnValidation()
helper.shouldsend205.role: Whether the validation of a received invoice must answer 205: the option, the invoice really coming from the platform, and no 205 already sent.

doc.reimport.label: Document::reimport()
doc.reimport.role: The way out of a bad import: delete the draft, sync the flow again, give the new invoice the reference of the draft it replaces, move the lifecycle history onto it, and adopt the row the import wrote so the flow keeps its line in the list.

doc.cleanxml.label: Document::cleanXmlData()
doc.cleanxml.role: Strips the attachments out of the received XML before it is stored, and checkXmlDataMaxSize() keeps it under the MEDIUMTEXT ceiling.

support.export.label: SupportExport
support.export.role: Packs the whole trail — flows, calls, links, statuses — into a support archive, replaying the redaction on rows written before it existed.
support.export.writes: a zip served to the operator

esalink.sendinvoice.label: Esalink sendInvoice()
esalink.sendinvoice.role: Deposits the file on hubtimize.fr/api/orchestrator/v1/: POST flows in multipart, then GET flows/{id}?docType=Metadata for the acknowledgement, with its own credentials and its own authentication.
esalink.sendinvoice.reads: the generated file in the invoice output dir, resolveFlowProfile()
esalink.sendinvoice.writes: insertOrUpdateExtLink() twice (AWAITING_VALIDATION, then the acknowledged status), addEvent(), logCall()

esalink.validatefile.label: Esalink validateEInvoiceFile()
esalink.validatefile.role: Esalink declares has_validator = 0, so hasValidator() is false: the automatic precheck never runs and no ap_precheck_* is ever written. Called by hand from the card it answers -1, NoAvailableValidatorforThisAccessPoint.
esalink.validatefile.writes: nothing: no ap_precheck_* is ever written for this provider

esalink.sendstatus.label: Esalink sendStatusMessage()
esalink.sendstatus.role: Checks the code is sendable for that object type, builds the CDAR with CdarHandler::generateCdarFile(), posts it as a flow of syntax CDAR, records it and reads back the platform verdict.

esalink.syncflows.label: Esalink syncFlows()
esalink.syncflows.role: Its flow search answers a total, so the run asks for that many rows in one call: no updatedAfter cursor to walk and no batch ceiling. Flows already stored are discarded, and an unreadable one is postponed.
esalink.syncflows.reads: POST flows/search, the total it returns
esalink.syncflows.writes: one Call row for the run; same postponeflow handling as SuperPDP

esalink.syncflow.label: Esalink syncFlow()
esalink.syncflow.role: Reads the flow metadata into a Document, dispatches on flow_type over the five flow types, and writes the Document row at the end whatever happened.

abstract.checkdirectory.label: AbstractPDPProvider::checkRecipientDirectory()
abstract.checkdirectory.role: The default directory lookup, kept by Esalink. A provider that exposes no directory keeps the 'unsupported' status, so the feature degrades instead of blocking.
abstract.checkdirectory.reads: the AFNOR directory of the provider

md: Nothing in the two chains is stateless: each step leaves a trace, and knowing which table holds what is half of any diagnosis.

rows: one **flow** of the PA (invoice or status, in or out)
the **PA state of one Dolibarr object**: syncstatus, flow_id, routing override, precheck
`fetchLastknownInvoiceStatus()`, `isTransmittedLockActive()`, the invoice list columns, the card blocks
one **lifecycle status message**, in or out, with its PA validation
`hasSentStatusMessage()`, `getSendableStatusesForReceivedInvoice()`, `fetchStatusMessages()`, the supplier invoice card and list
one **routing identifier** of a third party (`routing_type='thirdparty'`), or its default import product (`='product'`)
one **named property** the module keeps on a core object without using the core extrafields, which an admin could rename or delete
one **API call**, or one whole synchronization run, with its request and response, secrets redacted
the received document and the PA readable view
`getXmlData()`, the consistency check, the CDAR vendor identity

md: `import_key` on the supplier invoice holds `AbstractPDPProvider::$EINVOICING_LAST_IMPORT_KEY`, the timestamp of the synchronization run that created it — the one column that says "this batch".

md: The manual paths join the same chain further down, through the two shared helpers, so their gates can never diverge from the automatic one:
### What the document says, and where it comes from

`buildinvoicelines.inc.php` is the whole Dolibarr → EN 16931 mapping. Anything it does not fill simply does not exist in the transmitted document — which is why an audit of a missing field always starts in this file, never in `buildXML()`.

rows: not the same thing as BT-46 scheme 0224
preceding situation invoice, replaced invoice, deposit invoices
BT-31 or BT-32 per VAT regime
BT-49 = the routing of `llx_einvoicing_routing`, or the invoice-level override
the external BILLING contact of the invoice
names a party, not a person
earliest start, latest end of the line periods
the progress of a situation invoice is applied to the price
one breakdown per category + rate + exemption, never per `vat_src_code`
recomputed here, not read from the stored ones
`checkBusinessRules()` then confronts them with the invoice
A1 / A2 … decided by the invoice, not by an option

blocks.title: The three ways a status is emitted

steps.label: who fires, and on which invoice

branches.label: 212 Encaissee — on OUR OWN invoice (we are the seller)
lines: for each invoice paid by this payment, amount > 0
AUTOMATIC, no option: the reform wants every

branches.label: 205 Approuvee — on a SUPPLIER invoice (we are the buyer)
lines: or the card button, which validates the draft first
then sends only if the validation did not already

branches.label: 211 Paiement transmis — on a SUPPLIER invoice
SuperPDP
lines: is the code sendable for that object ?

branches.label: Esalink (Hubtimize)

md: Two return shapes matter and are easy to confuse:
* **error** (`res < 0`, no `postponeflow`): something *was* stored, or the flow is unusable. It is reported as a business action for the operator.

* **postponed** (`res < 0` **and** `postponeflow = 1`): nothing was stored, the flow stays pending and the next run retries it. Used when no readable document could be fetched, or when the invoice references a document Dolibarr does not hold yet. That flag is the reason one bad flow no longer stalls every invoice queued behind it.
